newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-SLEEPYTIME DEFEAT BRINGS CECIL DOWN TO EARTH.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-SLEEPYTIME DEFEAT BRINGS CECIL DOWN TO EARTH.

text.p: Henry Cecil and jockey Kieren Fallon, on top of the world after Bosra Sham's sparkling Royal Ascot victory on Tuesday, were brought down to earth swiftly on Wednesday.

Sleepytime, winner of the 1,000 Guineas and seen like Bosra Sham as a star filly, suffered a shock defeat in the Coronation Stakes at the hands of 25-1 outsider Rebecca Sharp, who had finished only 13th in the Guineas.
Sleepytime started the 5-6 favourite but could only finish third as Rebecca Sharp scored by three quarters-of-a-length over 16-1 chance Ocean Ridge, the mount of American Gary Stevens.
Sleepytime was another two lengths back in third, leaving Fallon to wonder if the ground was too riding too fast for the hot favourite.

Winning owner Anthony Oppenheimer confessed to having a "major doubt" about her chance on Wednesday but added: "We thought there must have been a problem in the Guineas but we could not find anything wrong."
The win was some consolation for trainer Geoff Wragg whose top class performer First Island, a Royal Ascot winner last year, died a few days ago following an operation.
The big handicap race of the meeting, the Royal Hunt Cup, went to Red Robbo, a 16-1 chance trained by Reg Akehurst and ridden by Frenchman Olivier Peslier, landing his second winner of the meeting.

In the opening Jersey Stakes, Michael Kinane, leading jockey at the royal meeting for the last three seasons, opened his account for 1997 when the 4-1 favourite Among Men scored by half a length from Godolphin challenger Kahal, ridden by Frankie Dettori.
Among Men is owned by Michael Tabor whose colt Entrepreneur proved a disappointing favourite in the Epsom Derby.
